speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful context. Given your recent start on risperidone, could you tell me if these movements appear as rigid stiffness, repetitive twisting motions, or rather involuntary, dance-like jerks? Also, do they worsen when you are stressed or anxious?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. Have you noticed any tremors in your hands or jaw clenching while you are trying to sit still? Also, are you experiencing any muscle spasms or difficulty swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Risperidone-induced akathisia. The clinical picture of severe inner restlessness, fidgeting, and an inability to remain still, occurring shortly after starting risperidone for schizophrenia, is classic for this extrapyramidal side effect. We do not need further imaging or extensive blood work at this time; the primary management will involve adjusting the antipsychotic dosage or adding a beta-blocker like propranolol.
